summary: Preserved candidate ea0cfb3's GLM5 bundled-NextN EAGLE3 rejection and closed its concrete same-checkpoint identity bypasses by comparing canonical local filesystem identity and Hub repo-plus-revision identity.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before reproduction: trailing-slash, literal-dot-component, and symlink spellings of the same existing local checkpoint were allowed by the candidate. Hugging Face validation also established that repo@revision is not a valid repo ID.

Passing-after regression and boundary coverage: 9 tests and 3 subtests passed for bundled local aliases, Hub default revision equivalence, distinct Hub revision allowance, algorithm and architecture boundaries, and existing GLM5 DFLASH capture behavior.
Trailing slash, literal dot component, symlink, and Hub None-vs-main identities were rejected; a distinct Hub revision remained allowed.
Patch whitespace validity and Python syntax.

gpu_evidence: The correction is startup path/revision identity logic and needs no GPU. No GLM-5.3 weights were available for a qualified architecture execution.
remaining_limitations: GLM-5.3-Flash weights and the reported 4x H20 TP=4 environment were unavailable.
No full server, CUDA fused_eh_norm, semantic accuracy, acceptance length, or throughput measurement was performed.
The original acceptance approximately 1.0 report remains unresolved.
No distinct GLM5 EAGLE3-trained draft was available, so its architecture compatibility and execution remain unverified.
The raw repo@revision spelling from review is not a valid Hugging Face repo ID; supported revision arguments were tested instead.
